expert_blurbs.author: DavisMattek
expert_blurbs.text: Highest projection of the slate in the highest total with a strong rushing projection. Caleb Williams is the definition of good chalk.

expert_blurbs.author: NeilCO
expert_blurbs.text: Eventually, losing Jack Campbell and Aidan Hutchinson will catch up to this defense.

expert_blurbs.author: Bobby Gomes
expert_blurbs.text: The Bears go to Detroit as 2.5-point road favorites in the game with the highest total on the slate at 55.5, and that environment is the whole case. Chicago leads the league in plays per game at 68, and Williams is averaging 247 passing yards with 10 touchdowns across seven starts while adding about 24 yards a game on the ground. Detroit has allowed the third-most passing yards per game and 21 passing touchdowns, tied for third-most in the league. The risk is pressure: the Lions are second in sacks with 36, and Williams has taken 16. He threw only 23 times against the Saints last week because Chicago was never pushed. I think this game pushes them, and at this price I want him as my lead quarterback.

players.notes: Excellent game enironment and all the weaponry is healthy.

expert_blurbs.author: vanekjordan
expert_blurbs.text: Goff has crushed Dennis Allen throughout his career, and this spot is another great one for him. The Bears' Jeffrey Simmons addition is awesome, but I think in the dome here the Lions beat them in the passing game.

players.notes: Great dome matchup and the price is outstanding for construction.
Highly concentrated target tree makes the stack easy to trust.
Lower owned than you'd expect thanks to a loaded slate.

expert_blurbs.author: ebeimfohr
expert_blurbs.text: On a very tricky small slate with one massively chalky game and a rough weather game, this "vomit stack" feels like one of the cleaner paths to winning tournaments. The Cowboys run defense is certainly worse than their pass defense, but the Eagles will be playing catch up with a healthy group of skill players alongside Milton. He offers some rushing floor and rushing TD upside alongside an instantly unique roster construction.

expert_blurbs.author: Bobby Gomes
expert_blurbs.text: 'll say the uncomfortable part first. Milton has not thrown a touchdown in his two starts, he's averaging 155 passing yards at under six yards an attempt, and he's been sacked 10 times. Philadelphia is implied for under 20 points as an 8.5-point underdog. So why play him? He's the cheapest starter on the slate in the softest matchup on it. Dallas has allowed the sixth-most passing yards per game and 21 passing touchdowns with just four interceptions, and the Eagles should be throwing from behind all afternoon. Milton has also run for 37 yards a game, which props up the floor. With DeVonta Smith back and seeing 12 targets last week, I think he's worth more exposure than the field will give him.

players.notes: Contrarian, but the Dallas defense is less than threatening.

expert_blurbs.author: headChopper
expert_blurbs.text: Buffalo ranks 23rd in schedule-adjusted fantasy points allowed to receivers, and with Kenneth Walker out, Kansas City's offense will lean even more on Mahomes.

players.notes: The offense is cooking, and the weather could really suppress ownership.

expert_blurbs.author: Bobby Gomes
expert_blurbs.text: He's the most expensive player on the slate and I think he's worth it. Gibbs is averaging 22 carries and 110 rushing yards a game with 13 rushing touchdowns, he's handled 85% of Detroit's running back carries, and his 29 carries inside the 10 are tied for the most in the league. He adds nearly six targets a game on top of that. Chicago's run defense has held up by volume, allowing 94 rushing yards a game, but it gives up 4.6 yards per carry, and I expect the receiving work to add to his line here. Detroit is at home in a game totaled at 55.5, and he's cleared 100 rushing yards five times in ten games. I don't want to be underweight on the best workload on the board.

players.notes: Elite workload with heavy carries and target volume in a 55.5-point game total.

expert_blurbs.author: Bobby Gomes
expert_blurbs.text: This one comes down to Kenneth Walker's groin. Walker returned to a limited practice Tuesday, and the Chiefs have said he remains the starter if he plays. If he sits again, Johnson is one of the best plays on the slate. In two starts he has handled 22 and 23 carries for 101 and 105 yards, caught 10 of 11 targets for 108 yards, and scored three times. That is a three-down workload at a mid-range price in a game with a 47.5 total. Buffalo has been middle of the pack against running backs, allowing the 13th-most DraftKings points to the position. If Walker is active I'm out, because the role shrinks to a handful of touches. If he's ruled out, I want to be well ahead of the field.

expert_blurbs.author: Krayton
expert_blurbs.text: It appears that Emmett Johnson may get the start once again and if he does, I will be locking him in every lineup just as I have done the last two weeks.  His price really only went up $1000 on both sites and for the production he is getting in this Chiefs lineup, he is still underpriced.  I will be watching this closely, however if Walker is out, Emmett Johnson is my favorite play on the slate.

players.notes: Three-down workhorse role offering immense value even at this price.
Continues to dominate the key roles with a combo of stablity and upside.
Monangai erodes the role, but Swift remains viable in a key game environment.

expert_blurbs.author: headChopper
expert_blurbs.text: Total GPP flyer here, but the last time these teams met a few weeks ago, Philly ran right through this defense with ease, and Barkley was dealing with injuries both before and during the game. Pollard just ripped off 100-plus rushing yards against Dallas, and there's a chance we see something similar happen again here.

players.notes: Tournament flyer with strong game script potential against Dallas run defense.
Cook has 10 TDS yet again, and with the weather, they could call his number all.

expert_blurbs.author: vanekjordan
expert_blurbs.text: Kyle Monangai is my favorite contrarian play on the slate. With Jack Campbell out, I expect Detroit to play more nickel and dime personnel, leaving them lighter up front. Monangai's physical running style is exactly what I want to attack that defensive structure. He's averaging 6.41 yards per carry with a 10% explosive run rate.

players.notes: Physical runner with high explosive rate facing a depleted Detroit front.
PPR upside as a lower-owned tournament pivot.
Will Shipley operates in a backup role for Philadelphia against Dallas.
Rare combination of volume and efficiency puts him in play every single week.

expert_blurbs.author: headChopper
expert_blurbs.text: Pickens has the far tougher boundary matchup in this game, but he's also significantly cheaper than CeeDee Lamb, and Dak isn't afraid to throw it up to Pickens, even in tough matchups.

players.notes: Dak is willing to throw jump balls to Pickens despite tough boundary matchups.

expert_blurbs.author: ebeimfohr
expert_blurbs.text: DeVonta was targeted on 12 of his 23 routes last week in his return, and Milton missed him wide open for a very long TD. We could see a boatload of targets even on limited route participation playing catchup against the Cowboys.

expert_blurbs.author: Bobby Gomes
expert_blurbs.text: Smith has played only five games, so the season totals undersell him. In those five he's averaged 10.6 targets and 70 yards, and he's accounted for 36% of Philadelphia's targets when active. He returned last week and drew 12 of Joe Milton's 21 pass attempts. The line was ugly, five catches for 41 yards, but that kind of volume is hard to find at this price. Dallas has allowed the fourth-most DraftKings points to wide receivers and 21 passing touchdowns, and the Eagles are 8.5-point underdogs, so the script should keep the ball in the air. The quarterback play caps the ceiling, and I won't pretend otherwise. I still think the target share is the best on the slate for the cost, and I'm going well over the field.

players.notes: Fully healthy and priced right, he could be primed for a smash.

expert_blurbs.author: Bobby Gomes
expert_blurbs.text: Burden has quietly become Chicago's lead receiver. He tops the team with 69 targets, a 22% share, and has 51 catches for 654 yards and four touchdowns. In the three games before last week he saw 4, 9 and 10 targets and scored in each. Then came a two-catch, 10-yard day against New Orleans in a game the Bears controlled, which should keep his ownership in check. Detroit has allowed the third-most passing yards per game, and the Lions have been more giving on the inside, where Burden does most of his work. In a game with a 55.5 total I expect Chicago to throw far more than 23 times. I prefer him to Rome Odunze as the receiver to pair with Caleb Williams, and I'm comfortable going back to him.

players.notes: Leads Chicago with a 22% target share operating inside against weaker defense.
Should be popular for good reason and seems to be matchup proof.

expert_blurbs.author: ebeimfohr
expert_blurbs.text: The weather is concerning, and Downs has not run a big share of the routes since coming to KC, but they are repeatedly targeting him when he's on the field. He has 9 targets on just 21 routes in 2 games, and they didn't really need to push him further in those easy wins. A huge matchup with the Bills could be the spot to unleash Downs, especially if the Chiefs are forced to be more aggressive, and he's going to get plenty of opportunity when he is on the field.

players.notes: Targeted heavily on limited routes and poised for aggressive usage.
We need cheap darts to throw on a 3 game slate, and he qualifies.
Deep tournament differentiator at a dirt cheap price.

expert_blurbs.author: DavisMattek
expert_blurbs.text: I don't like it, you do not like it but Worthy is the cheapest 80% snap share player on the entire 3 game Thursday slate.

players.notes: Cheapest 80% snap share receiver on the Thursday slate.
TD upside play deep down the board.

expert_blurbs.author: ebeimfohr
expert_blurbs.text: Loveland is re-emerging after a rough start to the season as a focal point of this Bears pass game, and the Lions have been an absolute sieve against opposing TEs.

expert_blurbs.author: Bobby Gomes
expert_blurbs.text: Detroit has been the best matchup in football for tight ends. The Lions have allowed 68 catches for 740 yards and 11 touchdowns to the position in ten games, the most DraftKings points in the league. Loveland is second on the Bears with 60 targets, a 19% share, and he leads the team with 12 red-zone targets. His box scores have been uneven, from 12 targets in one game to three last week against the Saints, which is the cost of an offense that spreads the ball. But this is the highest total on the slate, Chicago runs more plays than anyone, and he's the pass catcher I most want next to Caleb Williams. He's priced as the top tight end on the slate, and I think he earns it here.

players.notes: Leads the team with 12 red-zone targets against a weak Detroit tight end.

expert_blurbs.author: NeilCO
expert_blurbs.text: The Bears defense has given up the 2nd-most schedule-adjusted fantasy points per game to tight ends over the last five weeks.

players.notes: Anchors the Detroit tight end position in a high-total environment.

expert_blurbs.author: Krayton
expert_blurbs.text: This is actually a great TE slate as we have some elite options and I am liking some of my early builds with two TE's.  Kelce and Colston Loveland stand out as my two favorite TE options and Kelce is coming off of a big game against Arizona and he is a TE that is always capable of explosive games.

players.notes: Elite tight end option coming off a massive explosive game against Arizona.
Scored last week, and that would be more than enough on the 3-gamer.
Nice projection for the price, and ownership Will cluster around Loveland.
Punt TE for deep differentiaton.

expert_blurbs.author: Bobby Gomes
expert_blurbs.text: Knox is a salary play, and I want to be honest about how thin the season line is: 16 catches for 117 yards and a touchdown on 23 targets. The case is about this week. Dalton Kincaid missed last Sunday and was limited in practice Tuesday with thumb and ankle injuries, and Knox worked as Buffalo's lead tight end against Miami. Kansas City has been excellent against wide receivers and has allowed the fewest passing touchdowns in the league, but tight ends have been the soft spot: 69 catches for 646 yards and five scores, the sixth-most DraftKings points to the position. If Kincaid is out or limited, Knox gets Josh Allen's tight end looks at close to the minimum price. That's enough for me to take a position.

players.notes: Steps into lead tight end targets at near minimum price with Kincaid banged up.

expert_blurbs.author: DavisMattek
expert_blurbs.text: Both of the bad weather defenses are the best DST plays on the 3-game slate.
